Alan also provides viewers with some tips on sensory planting and creating home-made play equipment for children

The Sparrows have been running a boatyard for nearly 10 years, specialising in refurbishing and renting out floating homes to holidaymakers. Now they're designing and building a new, one-of-a-kind floating home for themselves - a futuristic-looking floating pod, drawing on a budget of £70,000

They begin by setting up home in a cottage as they wait for the arrival of their first livestock, and set out to prepare the ground for cropping by making tons of quicklime fertiliser to neutralise the acidity of the soil

event.name: Our Dream Farm with Matt Baker
event.description: Following the first elimination, six applicants now remain in the process, all hoping to secure the farm tenancy. With the ewes lambing, they need to be looked after at all hours. Matt introduces the next task - hosting a farm visit for a group of schoolchildren. Giles and Sally want to see the children learning about farming, conservation and food production, and of course, the children must have fun too

event.name: Edwardian Farm
event.description: Alex Langlands and Peter Ginn plough the land to plant potatoes and oats in an effort to secure some income, and are introduced to one of the Edwardian age's prime agricultural innovations - the tractor. Elsewhere, Ruth Goodman prepares for the arrival of the pigs by restoring an ingenious compost-maker, Peter starts to build a trout farm, and Alex learns to forge a billhook to maintain the hedgerows
